title: HEKATE Platform — ERP & Mobile App Specification
summary: One platform runs HEKATE: a web ERP hosted online and a mobile app on the same API, used by employees, clients and suppliers, with client support and incident handling at its centre.

sections.heading: Architecture

tables.Components: Clients and employees (mobile app, browser), suppliers (portal)
WAF + reverse proxy; VPN for admin access
Go API (single API for web and mobile); Next.js web ERP and portals; WebSockets + FCM push
PostgreSQL with row-level security (primary + replica); MinIO file storage; Metabase reporting
HCDP monitoring, logging, alerts; encrypted off-site backup
Static site on a separate host

content: Flow: every request passes the WAF, is authenticated by Keycloak, served by the Go API, and reaches data only through row-level security; nothing in the data layer is reachable from the internet.

sections.heading: Architecture style
content: Modular monolith, API-first, domain-driven and event-driven. One Go service split into strict domain modules; any module can be extracted into its own service without a rewrite when load justifies it.

tables.Rule: Modules are deployable units in waiting; extraction order: Support, Identity, Finance
Every endpoint defined in OpenAPI 3.1 before code; SDKs for web (TypeScript) and mobile (Dart) generated from the contract; contract tests in CI
Developer portal, API keys, plans, rate limits, `/v1` versioning, 12-month deprecation notice, usage metering for billing
Bounded contexts: CRM, Sales, Support & Incidents, Projects, Finance, Inventory & Assets, Procurement, HR, Documents, Identity, Platform. Each owns its schema; no cross-module table reads
Support & Incidents, Finance, Identity, dashboards: commands write to PostgreSQL, queries read from projections
Domain events (`ticket.created`, `invoice.paid`, `id.enrolled`) via transactional outbox to NATS JetStream; webhooks for external systems; idempotent consumers
Append-only, hash-chained records; no updates or deletes
Authorization Code + PKCE for web and mobile; Client Credentials for machine-to-machine; mTLS for government links; WebAuthn/TOTP two-factor
Roles and attributes in the token; tenant and row-level security enforced in PostgreSQL
Live chat and incident updates; FCM/APNs notifications

sections.heading: API conventions
items: REST over HTTPS, JSON, resource names in plural (`/v1/tickets`, `/v1/invoices`).
Cursor pagination, `Idempotency-Key` on every POST, ETags for concurrency.
Errors in RFC 9457 Problem Details format.
Every request carries a trace ID; every write lands in the audit log.
Rate limits per key and per tenant, returned in `RateLimit-*` headers.
Webhooks signed with HMAC-SHA256, retried with exponential backoff.

sections.heading: Public website and landing page
content: The public site (hekatesystems.com) is static and hosted separately from the ERP. Sections: hero with the client-portal sign-in, services, platform (ERP, support, identity), trust and security, sectors served, client support entry, contact, footer with verification link for HEKATE documents.

Company, founders, legal identity, values, locations
Enquiry form, emergency incident line, office map, departments
Tickets and incidents, quotes, invoices, contracts, reports, certificates, assets
Ticket queue, SLA timers, projects, timesheets, approvals, documents
Check any HEKATE document by QR or reference
Same functions, push notifications, offline drafts

sections.heading: Documents, forms and certificates in the platform
content: Every printable document built for HEKATE is a platform template. The platform fills it from live data, assigns the reference, signs it (PAdES), adds the QR verification code and logs it in the document register. Paper versions remain available for offline use.

Contract templates (NDA, Master Services Agreement and SLA, Data Processing Addendum, Pentest Authorisation and Rules of Engagement, Employment Contract, Screening Consent) are generated the same way from the Legal module.

Reference format: `HS-<CODE>-<YYYY>-<NNNNNN>`, with a `-<check>` character on certificates. Certificates carry the security features already built: guilloche, UV plate, hologram, microtext, Code128 barcode and signed QR.

tables.Name: Incident Report and Emergency Response Request

sections.heading: Guarantee policies
content: The full policy is in the separate document "HEKATE Guarantee Policies" (HS-GP). The platform enforces it: SLA timers on every ticket, automatic service credits on breach, warranty periods recorded against each delivery, and re-test entitlements tracked per engagement.

sections.heading: Responsive design
content: Every screen of the website, web ERP and portals is built mobile-first and desktop-complete: one fluid layout that adapts to any width from 320 px phones to 2560 px monitors, with no separate mobile site.
items: Fluid grids (CSS grid auto-fit, flex-wrap) and fluid type (clamp); breakpoints at 480, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1600 px.
Navigation collapses to a menu on phones; side menus stack above content; wide tables scroll inside their box.
Touch targets at least 44 px; no hover-only actions.
Tested on Android and iOS phones, tablets, laptops and large monitors in portrait and landscape.
The Flutter mobile app uses the same layouts and adapts to phone and tablet sizes.

sections.heading: Search and discovery optimisation
content: SEO, GEO (generative-engine optimisation) and AEO (answer-engine optimisation) are built into the public website from day one, not added later.
items: **SEO:** server-rendered pages, clean URLs, one H1 per page, meta titles and descriptions, XML sitemap, robots.txt, canonical tags, hreflang for English and French, Core Web Vitals targets (LCP under 2.5 s, CLS under 0.1, INP under 200 ms), image alt text, Google Business Profile for the Douala office.
**AEO:** FAQ sections on service pages with FAQPage schema, direct question-and-answer copy ("What does a penetration test cost in Cameroon?"), HowTo schema for support steps.

**GEO:** Organization, LocalBusiness and Service schema (JSON-LD) with legal name, RCCM, address and founders; consistent facts on every page; an llms.txt file; citable service and policy pages so AI assistants can quote HEKATE accurately.
Client portal, dashboards and ERP pages are excluded from indexing (noindex, behind sign-in).

sections.heading: Modules
content: Twelve modules share one database and one API; the website and client portal are views on the same data.

sections.heading: Users and roles
content: Every user sees only what their role allows, and clients and suppliers see only their own records.

tables.Can do: Everything, approvals above thresholds, all reports
Assigned tickets, interventions, timesheets, photos, client sign-off
Own leave, expenses, payslips, assets, notifications
Open tickets and incidents, chat, quotes, invoices, contracts, documents, verify certificates
Manage own company users, approve quotes
Answer RFQs, see POs, upload invoices, update bank details (with call-back check)

sections.heading: Mobile app
content: One app (Android and iOS) with two experiences chosen at login: staff and client. It talks only to the platform API, never to the database.
items: Report an incident in three taps: category, severity, description, photos or screenshots; urgent ones trigger the on-call engineer immediately
Open and follow support tickets with live status, SLA countdown and engineer assigned
Chat with support (text, files, voice notes); call-back request
Push notifications at each status change; rate the service when closed
Quotes to approve, invoices to pay (MTN MoMo, Orange Money, card), contracts and documents
Scan a HEKATE QR code to verify a certificate or document
Ticket queue, accept and update tickets, internal notes, escalation
Field interventions: check-in with GPS at client site, photos, parts used from stock, client signature on screen, auto-generated intervention report
Timesheets, leave and expense requests with receipt photos, payslips
On-call schedule and incident alerts
Works offline in the field and syncs when back online
Client reports by app, portal, e-mail (incident@hekatesystems.com) or phone; every channel becomes one ticket.
Ticket is classified by severity (P1 critical to P4 low); the SLA clock starts.
Auto-assigned to the right queue; P1 pages the on-call engineer and the Manager.
Engineer works remotely or on site; every action is logged.
Client confirms resolution in the app and rates it; a P1/P2 gets a written incident report.
SLA breaches and repeated incidents show on the management dashboard.

sections.heading: Technology stack and hosting
content: A custom build, generated with AI and reviewed module by module, on proven open-source parts and hosted on HEKATE's own servers.

tables.Why: Memory-safe, fast, small attack surface, one binary to deploy
One codebase for staff ERP, client and supplier portals
Nothing on the public site can reach the ERP
One codebase, offline support, good camera/GPS/signature support
Clients and suppliers can only read their own rows, enforced in the database
Single sign-on, two-factor login, roles in one place
Live ticket chat and push alerts

tables.Choice: 2 × DL380 Gen11 (app + API, active/standby), 1 × DL380 Gen11 (database primary), 1 × DL380 Gen10 (database replica + backups), 2 × DL380 Gen10 (monitoring/HCDP, test environment)
tables.Why: Uses the six servers in the RFQ; Proxmox virtualisation

tables.Choice: Encrypted nightly backup to a second location or cloud
tables.Why: Survives a fire or theft at the office

sections.heading: Security requirements
content: The platform must pass an internal and an external penetration test before go-live.
items: **Perimeter:** only the reverse proxy and web application firewall face the internet; the database and admin tools are reachable only through VPN.
**Login:** two-factor login for every staff account; passwordless or OTP for clients; account lockout and alerts on suspicious logins.
**Access:** role-based permissions plus database row-level security; every approval above the thresholds needs two people.
**Data:** TLS 1.3 everywhere; database and file storage encrypted at rest; personal data handled under Law 2024-017 and the Data Processing Addendum (HS-DOC-34).
**Mobile:** certificate pinning, no data stored unencrypted on the phone, remote logout of lost devices.
**Audit:** every create, change, delete and login logged and sent to HCDP; logs kept 12 months.
**Code:** automated tests, Semgrep code scanning and dependency scanning on every change; no code reaches production without review.
**Recovery:** daily encrypted backups, monthly restore test, target recovery within 4 hours.

sections.heading: Build plan
content: Support and incidents come first because clients feel them first; accounting comes last because it is the riskiest.

tables.Delivers: Specification, data model, login (Keycloak), servers and network
Clients, CRM, Support & Incidents (web + mobile app), public website
Projects & field service, quotations, invoicing, mobile payments

Two quarters run in parallel with the accountant's books
